# Unit 1 coverage audit — edition 0.5

> Historical editorial snapshot: original edition labels, dates and evidence statuses below are retained as provenance. Website edition 0.48 does not imply a new coverage review, learner evidence or teacher sign-off.

Reviewed 13 October 2026 against [SCSA Year 11 syllabus for teaching from 2026](https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0020/1232507/Computer-Science-ATAR-Year-11-Syllabus-for-teaching-from-2026.PDF), printed pages 8–13 (PDF pages 12–17), and [current support booklet v16](https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF). References below use printed syllabus page numbers. Labels are compact topic indexes, not reproduced syllabus wording. Consult the official documents for the complete requirements.

This is an editorial content map, not SCSA approval or proof of student mastery. “Present” means explanation plus a task/evidence opportunity exists; “Expanded” or “Added” identifies this revision. Knowledge and application are checked together where the syllabus repeats a concept under both. Student practical work, pacing and independent teacher review remain pending.

## Findings and corrections

- Added a software-responsibility chapter to the existing week 9 API/attribution lesson.
- Standardised assignment and explicit block endings in original pseudocode; replaced the informal fixed-repeat example with FOR.
- Added local/global tracing, test-last repetition, Boolean grouping and pseudocode for standard array algorithms.
- Added explicit file-mode practice and diagnostics for executed branches and variable values.
- Added LAN, WLAN and WAN diagram practice with an official-symbol checklist. Symbol fidelity must be judged visually by the teacher.
- Added four lessons of consolidation and four of exam preparation inside the existing weeks 15–16; no extra teaching weeks or weighted tasks.

## Checks still required before a classroom release

1. Teacher reviews technical depth, accepted answers and Cisco symbols against the linked official documents.
2. Students demonstrate implementation and debugging, project records, file processing and diagrams; written revision scores do not replace practical evidence.
3. Trial actual lesson length and school calendar. The allocation remains 16 × 4 = 64 teaching lessons; weeks 17–18 are blocked. Four lessons shorter than about 52 minutes require an hours review.
4. Independently review accessibility, ownership/licensing and content before public/open release. Original drafts are not automatically an openly licensed publication.

## Technical source record

- [Australian Government copyright basics](https://www.ag.gov.au/rights-and-protections/copyright/copyright-basics) and [permissions guidance](https://www.ag.gov.au/rights-and-protections/copyright/copyright-users): concepts in software responsibility; accessed 13 October 2026.
- [Open Source Initiative definition](https://opensource.org/osd): licence rights distinction; accessed 13 October 2026.
- Python documentation linked in the individual programming chapters; network chapter sources and official course conventions remain linked in the book.
